issues.detail: The Greek 'τὸ μὴ παρὼν θαρρῆσαι' means 'that when absent I may not be bold' (i.e., not having to be bold when present). The Vietnamese renders 'khi có mặt' ('when present'), reversing the meaning: it says 'when present, I may not have to use boldness,' whereas the Greek says 'when absent, [I pray] not to be bold' (i.e., that he won't need to be bold when he arrives). This reverses the temporal condition and changes the sense.
